title: Finite presentation and monomorphy of a closed subscheme inside a Noetherian open
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-pc-scheme]. Let $j:W\to S$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and let $i:C\to W$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $W$ is locally Noetherian. Each of $j$, $i$ and $q=j\circ i$ is a monomorphism of schemes (postcomposition with it is injective on every set of scheme morphisms). Each of these three morphisms is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation in the full convention [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. In particular, for every affine open $U\subseteq S$, $j^{-1}(U)$ and $q^{-1}(U)$ are quasi-compact. No separatedness hypothesis on $S$ and no reducedness hypothesis on $C$ is imposed.
